title: Lock-free SPSC ring buffers
hook: How does a single-producer single-consumer ring buffer work without a lock?

scenes.caption: A fixed array plus two counters: the producer owns tail, the consumer owns head.
scenes.narration: The ring is a fixed power-of-two array with two counters. Only the producer writes tail, and only the consumer writes head.

scenes.caption: Push: check space, write the slot, then publish it with a release-store of tail.
scenes.narration: To push, the producer checks for space, writes the slot, and only then publishes it with a release store of tail, so the consumer never sees an unwritten slot.

scenes.caption: Pop: acquire-load tail, read the slot, then release-store head so the producer may reuse it.
scenes.narration: Pop mirrors it. The consumer acquire-loads tail, reads the slot, then release-stores head, which tells the producer the slot is free to reuse.

scenes.caption: Counters grow forever and are masked with N-1; unsigned wraparound keeps tail - head correct.
scenes.narration: Counters grow without bound and are masked with N minus one. Unsigned wraparound keeps tail minus head correct, so empty and full are easy to tell apart.

elements.text: Put head and tail on separate cache lines to avoid false sharing.

scenes.caption: Real users: kfifo, io_uring, perf's mmap buffer, virtio vrings. Multiple producers need CAS.
scenes.narration: The pattern is everywhere: kfifo, the io_uring rings, perf's mmap buffer and virtio vrings. Multiple producers or consumers need compare-and-swap instead.

takeaway: With one writer per counter and release/acquire pairs, a ring buffer needs no lock and no read-modify-write.
